title: Navitas Q4 Revenue Guide Tops Estimates as Company Pivots to AI Infrastructure
summary:
The power semiconductor manufacturer reported $14 million in third-quarter revenue, beating the $13.2 million projection. Navitas saw its non-GAAP gross margin reach 40% and adjusted earnings per share come in at -$0.03 per share, compared with estimates of 39.4% and -$0.04, respectively. The company issued fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $16 million, plus or minus $500,000, which is higher than the $14.7 million analyst consensus.

The financial results come as Navitas pivots away from the mobile and low-end consumer markets to prioritize AI data centers and energy grid infrastructure. The company expects AI infrastructure to make up more than 40% of its sales by the end of 2026. To support this shift, Navitas recently acquired Claros for its grid-to-xPU technology and is developing 800V power board solutions for Nvidia and 10 kV silicon carbide semiconductors for the U.S. government.

NAVITAS SEMICONDUCTOR $NVTS Q3’26 EARNINGS HIGHLIGHTS

🔹 Revenue: $14.0M (Est. $13.2M) 🟢; +38% YoY
🔹 Adj. EPS: -$0.03 (Est. -$0.04) 🟢
🔹 Non-GAAP Gross Margin: 40.0% (Est. 39.4%) 🟢; +130 bps YoY

Q4 Guide:
🔹 Revenue: $16.0M +/- $0.5M (Est. $14.7M) 🟢
🔹 Non-GAAP Gross Margin: 40.5% +/- 100 bps (Est. 39.8%) 🟢

Announcements:
🔹 NVIDIA: 800 V-to-12 V board; 800 V-to-6 V and 800 V-to-50 V solutions
🔹 U.S. Government: Selected to develop next-generation 10 kV SiC semiconductors

Other Q3 Metrics:
🔹 High-Power Revenue Growth: 125% for FY26
🔹 AI Infrastructure: More than 40% of total sales by year-end

Key Updates:
🔹 Claros acquisition closed, adding IVR technology for the grid-to-xPU strategy

Comments:
🔸 “By year-end, we expect mobile and low-end consumer revenue to be essentially eliminated from our mix, further positioning the Company as a high-power business with AI Infrastructure, composed of AI Data Centers and energy grid infrastructures that power them, expected to account for more than 40% of total revenue.”

🔸 “At the midpoint of our fourth quarter guidance, we expect to deliver the fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit sequential revenue growth and exit 2026 as a high-power company with a strong book-to-bill ratio well above one and backlog that extends into mid-2027.”
